agree.reason: A long-serving teller who doesn't want phone work gets a concrete reason to try the role: they can keep their severance if they leave within six months, they get seniority-based shift choice and a $1.50 raise. But the letter never mentions the two weeks of rumours, and it says nothing about what the phone work itself is like.

honest.reason: The letter rightly drops the 'better for everyone' claim, but it invents 'I don't know of any plans to close others' and calls the phone team 'substantially bigger' when the brief gives no team size. It also says contacts rose 'every year' when the brief only gives a three-year total.

works_the_facts.reason: The given figures are restated rather than worked out: there is no annual value for the $1.50 an hour (about $3,100 for full-time staff) and no severance example for a ten-year employee (20 weeks' pay), which is what these readers would most want to see.

right_comparison.reason: Taking severance is laid out clearly as the alternative, and the falling branch visits are presented as a trend. But the letter doesn't say plainly that keeping the branch job is not an option, and it doesn't show what nine-minute hold times would become if nothing changed.

qualification.reason: The commitments come with dates readers can check (offers by February 14, decision by March 1, a six-month window with severance as the consequence). The made-up hedge about other closures can't be checked.

objections.reason: The main objections — not wanting phone work, losing 9-to-5 hours and the phone team's turnover — are each met with something concrete. The rumours these readers have already heard go unacknowledged.

fit.reason: It is an email from the COO with a subject line, at about 430 words against the requested 400. Leaving the '[Your name]' placeholder when the writer knew the COO's name is a small flaw.
